chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ghayath (mursal), and Sa'd narrated from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ghayath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah, from Ali (peace be upon him):
"He used not to raise his hands in the Janazah (funeral prayer) except once, meaning in the Takbir."

key_terms.التَّكْبِير: The act of saying 'Allahu Akbar' (God is Greater), specifically referring to the opening declaration in prayer
key_terms.يَرْفَعُ يَدَهُ: To raise his hand (a ritual action during prayer)

ai.seo_question: How many times are hands raised during the funeral prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights a specific juristic preference (khas) in Shia fiqh regarding the ritual of funeral prayer, distinguishing the single hand-raising from the multiple instances found in other prayers. By tracing the chain back to Imam al-Sadiq and ultimately Imam Ali, it underscores the continuity of this practice within the Ahl al-Bayt's tradition, offering a nuanced view on the physical etiquette (adab) of the Janazah. This ruling reflects the scholarly emphasis on adhering to the Prophetic and Imami precedents in acts of worship that lack explicit, detailed scriptural instruction.
